Pravin Probed 2

By: Graham Coetzer | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After denials from government, the Hawks and the NPA, it seems that the state is now preparing to arrest Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan - we probe the implications.

Unique Selling Point:
In our previous story earlier this year, government and the authorities denied an ongoing investigation into finance minister Pravin Gordhan. But with the minister and several former SARS rogue unit role players ordered to report to the Hawks tomorrow morning, it seems the state is finally ready to show there cards and the implications for the country are obviously enormous.

Summary:
We will be speaking to economists, political analysts and unpacking the story.

Expert:
Mr. Iraj Abedian
Prof. Mcebisi Ndletyana

NO PRESSER RELEASED... (One-liner - After denials from government, the Hawks and the NPA, it seems that the state is now preparing to arrest Finance Minister Pravin Gorhan - we probe the implications.)

Script:


Final Pravin Probed 2

Voice
On Thursday morning this week former SARS commissioner Ivan Pillay and High Risk Investigations unit head Johan van Loggerenberg reported to the Hawks offices at the Piet Joubert building in downtown Pretoria to receive warning statements from the cops. (15sec17f)

Sound Up Johan van Loggerenberg
Thank you very much. Not just for the people who came but also for the people who continually send us messages. It is wonderful. I have received thousands of messages since yesterday. Thank you very much.

Voice
Absent from the media spotlight was Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan, who to declined the Hawks summons to their offices. (7sec17f)

Sound Up Pravin Gordhan
I therefore do not intend to present myself for a warning statement for many considerations, both legal and given my other commitments.

Voice
If the Hawks want to obtain a warning statement from you it means you are officially a suspect in an ongoing investigation, which after months of speculation and denials, the finance minister has now become. (12sec16f)

Sound Up Pravin Gordhan
I am advised by my legal team that the assertions of law made by the Hawks in their letter of 21 August 2016 are wholly unfounded on any version of the facts.

Voice
The minister’s legal game of chess with the Hawks started earlier this year when he received a list of 27 questions pertaining to the so-called Sars rogue spy unit from Hawks boss General Berning Ntlemeza just days before his budget speech. (16sec07f)

Sound Up Pravin Gordhan
…Allegations that are unfounded, based on leaked documents that even I have not seen…

Voice
The move by the Hawks caused a media frenzy as speculation of the minister’s imminent arrest sparked fears of economic and political turmoil. In June this year Carte Blanche reported on leaked documents indicating the minister was still under investigation. (15sec17f)

Sound Up Abram Mashego
Bongani: So it specifically tells the State Security Minister that his cabinet colleague is a person of interest to the Hawks?

Abram: Correct

Voice
At the time the Hawks, the Minister of Police and the ruling party denied the allegations. (5sec24f)

Sound Up Gwede Mantashe
Minister Gordhan is the minister of finance, we have repeatedly said you have our support; the president came out and said you have our support, the NPA came out and said there is no prosecution against him that is what we are taking as the ANC.

Link John
For some time the country was distracted by the local government elections, but with the results announced and the new councils sworn in, suddenly the SARS wars are back in the headlines.

Voice
The questionable timing of the Hawks moves and the cloak and dagger game they’ve played with minister Gordhan over the past year mobilized civil society to come to his defense this week. (11sec08f)

Sound Up Francis Antonie
We’ve seen persecution like this previously in this country, only some short twenty years ago. Have we come back to this point where senior officials, doing their job, are persecuted for certain political aims.

Voice
Francis Antonie from the Helen Suzman foundation was one of the eminent people showing their support outside the Hawks offices on Thursday. Also present was former constitutional court judge Johann Kriegler and advocate George Bizos. (13sec19f)

Sound Up George Bizos
We stand by the minister of finance, we hope that the people of South Africa will stand by him, and that this prosecution is nipped in the bud.

Voice
The current investigation relates back to 2007 when Pravin Gordhan was the commissioner of SARS. He oversaw the formation of an intelligence-gathering unit within the revenue service, which would probe dodgy taxpayers. The High Risk Investigations Unit, as it was eventually called, would later be accused of going rogue, allegations that have never been proven. (24sec09f)

Sound Up Johann Kriegler
The idea of the rogue unit, we know where it comes from, it has no substance whatsoever. The minister has gone on record, it is perfectly clear that it is an investigative unit such as any revenue gathering organization needs.

Link John
Much of the controversy around the so-called SARS wars has focused on the political impact, but there are others who argue that the most lasting and damaging effect will be to the economy.

Sound Up Dr Iraj Abedian
The South African economy is literally on a knife-edge. In the age of digital information, instantaneous access to not only facts, but access to speculations, you cannot run a modern economy in this way.

Voice
Economist doctor Iraj Abedian says the Rand fell by almost 5 percent this week as markets reacted negatively to the events surrounding the finance minister. (10sec17f)

Sound Up Iraj
Even if there is a real issue, because of that access to information and digital age, you manage it differently. With full concern and respect for South African brand and national interest.

Sound Up Francis
Having looked at all the documentation that has been put into the public realm I can see no basis for this sort of initiative. Other then to intimidate people both in SARS and in the treasury, but especially in the treasury.

Voice
After about 4 hours of grilling by the Hawks, Ivan Pillay and Johann van Loggerenberg emerged from the offices looking calm and relaxed. They declined to comment on the nature of the allegations against them. (11sec23f)

Sound Up Johan van Loggerenberg
No as I say let’s stick to what my attorney said and that’s what we are prepared to say for now.

Voice
Their attorney Robert Levine said there were no charges against his clients, only allegations. (06sec14f)


Sound Up Robert Levine
Out clients will be following due process. They consider the allegations baseless and they will be addressing their due process in accordance with their rights.

Voice
Judge Kriegler has not only questioned the Hawks handling of the case thus far, but also the appointment of General Berning Ntlemeza at the head of the unit after the controversial ousting of former chiefs Anwar Dramat and Shadrack Sibiya. (13sec16f)

Sound Up Judge
Good honest cops being forced out of office on trumped up, rubbish charges. I personally have read the records of both those proceedings. I have no hesitation in saying it is impossible to have found them guilty as they were. They were forced out of office, they were replaced by a man of doubtful capacity and doubtful integrity.

Voice
This week saw everyone from big business to academics calling for transparency in the investigation, and a lot of the backlash was aimed at president Zuma. (08sec22f)

Sound Up Mark Heywood
I personally think that it is happening now because the local government elections are out of the way, because Jacob Zuma got a bloody nose and he is wounded and he knows that he is wounded

Sound Up Wayne Duvenhage

Voice
Iraj says it will ultimately be the man on the street who suffers the most should minister Gordhan be removed from his position right now. (07sec08f)

Sound Up Iraj
The rich may lose 10% of their wealth. But the rich and the bourgeoisie survive no matter what. Their subsistence is never at risk. For the working class and the poor, their very subsistence becomes an issue. Not for a month or six months, for five to seven years.

Link John
The president has emphasized that he is not in a position to interfere in a criminal matter, but civil society groups say that because of it’s impact on the economy in particular, this is an issue that is crying out for leadership of one kind or another.

Sound Up Professor Mcebisi Ndletyana
If you have a decision that affects the health of the country as a whole, surely that decision is discussed with the president and the president should have a say in whether or not that is good.

Voice
Mcebisi Ndletyana is an associate professor of political science at the University of Johannesburg. He says the lack of leadership displayed in the SARS wars saga is unacceptable. (11sec12f)

Sound Up Prof
We are not saying that Pravin Gordhan is above the law, but surely there are ways of doing these things without necessarily making a mess of them, without necessarily endangering the future of the country.

Voice
The Hawks have not responded to our requests for comment, and while no man is above the law, the investigation into the minister of finance seems to have raised more questions than answers. (11sec10f)

Sound Up Judge Kriegler
Judge: The question is why are all of these state institutions being undermined and their competent decent people being worked out.

John: And what is the answer to that question, why?

Judge: I don’t know. But what I do know is that it is extremely serious. And extremely worrisome to every decent South African.

Voice
In December South Africa will once again face the possibility of a ratings downgrade. The longer the cat and mouse games continue, the closer we get to the economic abyss. (10sec02f)

Sound Up Iraj

Voice
So perhaps for now at least, the authorities would be wise to take a word of advice from the minister himself. (07sec 03f)

Sound Up Pravin
-I have a job to do in a difficult economic environment and to serve South Africa as best I can. Let me do my job.
